environment: Humpback highway hits its spring peak with record calf sightings off the Queensland coast
Community mangrove planting day on Moreton Bay ties a personal best for volunteer numbers
science: Queensland researchers unveil a hardier strain of coral showing real promise for reef recovery
sports: Grassroots footy grand final fever sweeps the south east as junior clubs crown their spring champions
stories.overview: Stargazers across the south east catch a rare clear-sky show as spring skies put on their best display of the year

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, it's Thursday the twenty fourth of September and mate, there is a lot of good to get through. I'm Alex Mercer, sitting here with my partner in good news, Jamie. Morning Alex, and morning to all of you tuning in from up and down the coast. We have got whales, we have got coral, and we have got a sky show that had half of south east Queensland out on their back lawns last night. Plus Sam's got the weather sorted for your weekend plans, and we will finish up with some proper grassroots sporting spirit. Let's get into it, starting with the green stuff, as always.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Alex, it is peak whale season out there and the humpback highway is absolutely chocka this year. Spotters along the coast are reporting some of the highest calf numbers in years, which is a ripper sign for the population bouncing back. Yeah I saw a clip of one breaching off the Gold Coast yesterday, closest thing to a proper miracle you will see before your morning coffee. Big tail slap, kids on the beach going off, the whole show. And closer to home, volunteers down on Moreton Bay just wrapped up a mangrove planting day that matched their best ever turnout. Hundreds of hands in the mud for a few hours, and thousands more little seedlings in the ground doing the hard yards for our coastline.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Righto Jamie, science time, and this one is close to home for us reef lovers. Queensland researchers have been working on a tougher, more heat resistant strain of coral, and early results are looking genuinely promising. It is basically giving the reef a bit of extra armour for the warmer summers we keep copping. The scientists reckon it is not a silver bullet, but it buys precious time for the reef while the bigger climate work gets done. Love that, patient science doing the unglamorous heavy lifting. No fireworks, just years of lab work quietly paying off for something we all love swimming over.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and good on you all for putting up with me again. Spring is well and truly strutting its stuff across the south east this week, with clear skies and light winds making for an absolute cracker of a Thursday. Brisbane is looking at sunshine and a top around twenty five, the Gold and Sunshine Coasts a touch milder near the water with that lovely afternoon sea breeze kicking in. We will hold onto the dry and settled pattern right through the weekend, so if you have got the boat, the barbecue or just a picnic rug planned, you are in the box seat. Only thing to watch is those cooler mornings, so rug up early before the sun does its job. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Now Jamie, forget the big league finals for a tick, because the real drama this week has been happening on suburban ovals right across the south east. Junior footy grand finals wrapped up over the weekend and mate, the sportsmanship on display was next level. I heard about that under twelves side that lost the decider but still lined up to guard-of-honour the winners off the ground. That is the kind of thing that makes you proud of grassroots sport, no egos, just kids loving the game. Exactly, and every one of those clubs runs on volunteers, snag sizzles and parents washing muddy jumpers at midnight. Massive shout out to every coach and canteen legend who made this finals season happen.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: So there you have it, whales putting on a show, coral getting a fighting chance, and our juniors showing the big leagues how it is done. Not a bad Thursday for good news if you ask me. Honestly one of my favourite editions, and that sky show last night was just the cherry on top. If you managed to get a photo, we would love to see it. Big thanks to Sam for keeping us dry and sunny this weekend, and to all of you for tuning in and being part of the Bright Side family. Get out there and enjoy that spring sunshine. That is it from us today. Look after each other, look after the coastline, and we will catch you tomorrow with more of the good stuff. Too easy. From Alex, Jamie and Sam, this has been ParkSyde Bright Side, see you next time.
